title: Miwok Material Culture: Indian Life of the Yosemite Region (1933), “Music,” by S. A. Barrett and E. W. Gifford
text: The musical instruments of the Miwok were few and simple. The foot drum used in the assembly house has been described. Double and single bone whistles (mi'kūya'ke, P; kūya'ke, N) were used in dances (plate LVII, figs. 1-8). An elder whistle was used by Central Miwok shamans in curing the sick, and by dancers among the Southern Miwok (Field Museum 70203).
